patterns.title: إنه احنا، نكتب -> إنه احنا بنكتب
patterns.why: After enno the b- is KEPT (B3); he dropped it (نكتب) in a plain-present statement 'the second problem is that we write...'; Amal answered مم-هم (16:11) and let it pass. Best reading.

patterns.title: جو -> الجو (شوب)

The adjective شوب is absent in the transcript but she answered عن جد؟ as if she heard a complete statement, so the missing word is likely an ASR drop and is not scored - only the el- is. B reading.

patterns.why: رن takes على (sheet: i call | Ana barenn (3ala) | أنا برن); he used لـ and she let it pass - he then got lost hunting for 'electricity' and she followed that (08:51). B reading.

patterns.title: ما يكون -> مش
patterns.why: Saying who the man he called is - 'he is not a kahrabji, he is an engineer' - is a present noun predicate: Levantine negates it with مش and no 'to be' (C4); ما يكون is neither that nor a licensed ykoon context (B8: only after lamma/iza or for habits). The man's job is a present fact, so ما كان (r2) is not the target either. She said nothing about it; her 10:30 صلح لي moves to his next clause.
